deities: Devi (Yoginis); main back-wall cell presumed a Durga shrine

history.dynasty: Early Chandela (attribution from style; no foundation inscription found)
history.summary: The Chausath Yogini temple is the oldest surviving temple at Khajuraho, dated to about 885 CE. Unlike the other yogini temples of India, which are circular, it is an open-air (hypaethral) rectangular courtyard of 67 small granite cells — the only Khajuraho temple built entirely of granite and the only one facing north. Of the 67 cells, 35 survive; the large cell in the centre of the back wall is presumed to have been the main shrine (probably Durga). Three surviving sculptures — Brahmani, Mahesvari and Hingalaja (Mahishamardini) — are among Khajuraho's oldest and are kept in the archaeological museum. The temple is an ASI Monument of National Importance and part of the 1986 UNESCO World Heritage listing of the Khajuraho Group of Monuments. NOTE: because no inscription names a builder, some sources suggest it predates or is not Chandela work (verify). Coordinates approximate (ruin site).

name: Chausath Yogini Temple, Khajuraho
town_description: Khajuraho is a small town in Chhatarpur district, Madhya Pradesh, world-famous for its group of 9th–11th century Hindu and Jain temples built by the Chandela dynasty. The temple complex is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, drawing visitors for its Nagara architecture and intricate sculpture. The town is a compact tourist hub with hotels, the Khajuraho Dance Festival grounds, and an ASI archaeological museum.
